figures.finding: Guam's income tax follows the United States: Guam has its own tax system using the same tax laws and rates as the US (the mirror Guam Territorial Income Tax), administered by Guam's Department of Revenue and Taxation; a bona fide resident files only with Guam on worldwide income.

value.administeredBy: Guam Department of Revenue and Taxation

figures.applies: 2026. Rates, brackets, the standard deduction and dates are those of the US entry (the Guam Territorial Income Tax mirrors the US Internal Revenue Code).

sources.said: Guam Guam has its own tax system based on the same tax laws and tax rates that apply in the United States.

If you are a bona fide resident of Guam during the tax year, file your return with Guam. This applies to all bona fide residents who are citizens, resident aliens, or nonresident aliens of the United States. Include income from worldwide sources on your Guam return.
Section 6011(e)(2)(a) of the Guam Territorial Income Tax Code

figures.finding: Social security follows the US: a bona fide resident with self-employment income pays US self-employment tax (social security and Medicare) to the United States, and employees pay US FICA.
figures.applies: 2026; rates and wage base are the US entry's.

sources.said: Bona fide residents of a U.S. territory who have self-employment income must generally pay self-employment tax to the United States. Self-employment tax includes both social security and Medicare.
